::: {#rem-implies-terms}
#### Names for the parts, and other notation

In $P \Rightarrow Q$,
$P$ is the *premise* (also called the *hypothesis* or *antecedent*)
and $Q$ is the *conclusion* (also called the *consequent*).
A proposition of this form is also called a *conditional* or an *implication*.

Many textbooks write $P \rightarrow Q$ for $P \Rightarrow Q$.

:::
